overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating by email and voting on search committee appointments outside a posted meeting, but not intentionally; it ordered compliance and release of the chair's email.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee deliberated outside a posted meeting about which members would serve on a superintendent search committee.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Chair DiGiacomo violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a posted meeting via email on January 19.

allegations.summary: Committee voted to appoint members to the search committee outside a posted meeting, which the committee admitted.
allegations.key_passage: Moreover, the Committee admits, and we agree, that it violated the Open Meeting Law when the Committee voted to appoint members to the Search Committee outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the violation was intentional, which would raise the penalty under the law.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find no evidence that the Committee intentionally violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Request for further review raised allegations drawn from public records requests about emails, which were not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review any additional allegations made in the request for further review based on Ms. Crossman’s public records requests.

allegations.summary: Request for further review alleged four members' attendance at a Finance Committee meeting was improper, but this was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: as those allegations were not contained in the original complaint

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

Publicly release the Chair's January 19 email within 30 days of receipt of the determination, by reading it at a meeting and listing it in the minutes, or by posting it with the minutes on the municipal website.
remedy_passage: In addition, we order the Committee, to publicly release the Chair’s January 19 email discussed above within 30 days of receipt of this determination.
